Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.description: Find RPC handlers causing outbound HTTP
input.prompt:
In this repository, I need to find RPC handler methods that can transitively cause an outbound HTTP request to a user-configured URL (e.g., webhook URLs, integration URLs, custom endpoints configured by a user), and the single function where those different code paths converge before actually making the HTTP request (e.g., a shared "sendWebhook" / "doRequest" / "fetch wrapper" function).

Please:
1. Search for RPC handler definitions (look for directories/files with "rpc", "handlers", "api" in the name, or Connect/gRPC/tRPC-style service implementations).
2. Search for outbound HTTP call sites - grep for things like `http.Post`, `http.Client`, `fetch(`, `axios`, `request(`, `httpClient`, `webhook`, etc.
3. Trace which RPC handlers can reach a piece of code that sends an HTTP request to a URL that comes from user configuration (e.g., a webhook URL stored in a database, an integration config, a custom notification URL).
4. Identify the single shared/convergence function where these different paths meet before actually issuing the HTTP request (e.g. a common "send" or "deliver" or "post" helper).

Report back:
- At least 3 RPC handler method names with their file paths and line numbers
- The convergence function name, file path, and line number
- Brief explanation of the call chain from each handler to the convergence function

Be precise with file paths and line numbers since I need to cite them.

User-configured webhook URLs are stored per-user (`storepb.WebhooksUserSetting_Webhook.Url`) and fetched via `store.GetUserWebhooks` (`/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go:312`). Several RPC handlers, after mutating a memo, look up the calling user's configured webhooks and dispatch an HTTP POST to each one.

### Convergence function

**`Post`** — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`
```go
func Post(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) error {
```
This is the single place that actually builds and issues the outbound `http.Request` (`req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", requestPayload.URL, ...)` at line 126) via the shared `safeClient` (`http.Client` defined at line 32) and executes it at `safeClient.Do(req)` (line 152). `requestPayload.URL` comes straight from the user's stored webhook config.

All async dispatch paths funnel through **`PostAsync`** — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`, which enqueues the payload on `asyncPostQueue` (line 39); four worker goroutines started in `init()` (lines 42-55) pull from that queue and call `Post` (line 46). 1. **`CreateMemo`** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70`
   Calls `s.DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage)` at line 157 → `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (`memo_service_webhooks.go:48`) → loads `s.Store.GetUserWebhooks(ctx, creatorID)` (line 57) → for each hook, sets `payload.URL = hook.Url` (line 67) and calls `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` (line 71) → `Post`.

2. **`UpdateMemo`** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401`
   Calls `s.dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects(...)` at line 513 (`memo_update_helpers.go:66`), which calls `s.DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage)` at line 67 → `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (`memo_service_webhooks.go:48`) → `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` (line 71) → `Post`.

   Calls `s.DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage)` at line 562 → `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (`memo_service_webhooks.go:48`) → `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` (line 71) → `Post`.

4. **`CreateMemoComment`** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20`
   Calls `s.DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook(ctx, memoComment, relatedMemo.CreatorID)` at line 119 → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (`memo_service_webhooks.go:30`) → `s.Store.GetUserWebhooks(ctx, relatedMemoCreatorID)` (line 31) → for each hook, `payload.URL = hook.Url` (line 41), `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` (line 43) → `Post`.

### Call chain diagram

```
CreateMemo (memo_service.go:70)
UpdateMemo (memo_service.go:401)
SetMemoAttachments (memo_attachment_service.go:16)
SetMemoRelations (memo_relation_service.go:16)
DeleteMemo (memo_service.go:518)
CreateMemoComment (memo_service_comments.go:20)
        │
        ├─> DispatchMemo{Created,Updated,Deleted}Webhook /
        │   dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects /
        │   DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook   (memo_service_webhooks.go / memo_update_helpers.go)
        │        │
        │        ├─> store.GetUserWebhooks()  (store/user_setting.go:312)  -- fetches user-configured URL
        │        │
        │        └─> webhook.PostAsync(payload)  (internal/webhook/webhook.go:184)
        │                 │
        │                 └─> asyncPostQueue -> worker goroutine -> webhook.Post(payload)
        │
        └────────────────────────────>  webhook.Post  (internal/webhook/webhook.go:120)  <-- CONVERGENCE
                                              │
                                              └─> http.NewRequest + safeClient.Do(req)  (lines 126, 152)
```

Note: `webhook.go` also implements SSRF protection via `safeDialContext` (line 59) as a defense specifically because `Post`'s destination URL is user-supplied — reinforcing that this is the intended single choke point for all outbound webhook traffic.</result>
